text.root.agentsFile.3: This repository is {name}{value}, a living, AI-readable second brain. These instructions apply to every task in this repository.
text.root.agentsFile.4: Before working, read {index}, {recallMap}, and the relevant project Capsule. Expand into the Hub, Context, Decisions, Rules, or specialized memory only when needed.
text.root.agentsFile.5: Treat {name} as the source of truth. Prefer the latest explicit correction from {name2} and the most specific project file when information conflicts.
text.root.agentsFile.6: When interpreting {name}'s preferences, project ownership, communication style, or admin-level corrections, read {adminProfile}.
text.root.agentsFile.7: Complete the requested work without inventing missing project facts.
text.root.agentsFile.8: At the end of the task, determine whether durable memory changed.
text.root.agentsFile.9: If durable memory changed, update the relevant Markdown files: Context for identity and scope, Decisions for confirmed choices and corrections, Rules for future behavior, and specialized files for domain memory.
text.root.agentsFile.10: Put uncertain or unconfirmed information under `Needs Confirmation`; do not record it as fact.
text.root.agentsFile.11: After changes, run `vulcanus doctor` and require it to pass.
text.root.agentsFile.12: Then run `vulcanus sync "short topic"` to commit and push when `origin` is configured.
text.root.agentsFile.13: Report whether memory changed, the files changed, the validation result, commit hash, push status, and any `Needs Confirmation` items.
text.root.agentsFile.14: If no durable memory changed, do not edit {name} merely to create activity. Report `update not needed` with a brief reason.
text.root.agentsFile.15: Update {name} for durable project definitions, scope, decisions, corrections, constraints, reusable implementation patterns, architecture choices, workflows, visual rules, or knowledge that should change future AI behavior.
text.root.agentsFile.16: Do not update it for casual chat, repeated explanations, one-off commands, temporary debugging, unconfirmed guesses, or failed experiments unless they become a reusable rule or confirmed decision.
text.root.agentsFile.17: Start with {recallMap} and the relevant Capsule.
text.root.agentsFile.18: Only read full Context, Decisions, and Rules when the Capsule does not provide enough authority or detail.
text.root.agentsFile.19: Use deep recall for architecture, scope, rules, visual identity, legal or content constraints, algorithms, safety behavior, or durable memory changes.
text.root.agentsFile.20: Read specialized files only when their domain is directly relevant.
text.root.agentsFile.21: If the minimum layer resolves a low-risk task, do not load the entire project cluster.
text.root.agentsFile.22: When uncertain or when sources conflict, move to the next layer and prefer the latest explicit correction and the most specific file.
text.root.agentsFile.23: After work, check whether durable knowledge requires updates to the Capsule, Recall Map, Context, Decisions, Rules, or a specialized file. Also check whether older information should be deprecated and whether unresolved items belong under `Needs Confirmation`.
